correctness.rationale: I.i.d. atomless order representation makes each signed r-window probability exactly 1/r!; all overlapping joint probabilities follow from the explicit shared-order classification, including the one-point opposite-sign extremum. Their summed mass vanishes when n/r! tends to positive finite lambda. Independent blocks of length floor(n^(1/3)) retain all rare events with probability 1-o(1) and give marked spatial Poisson convergence. In the same blocks the Lindeberg CLT for bounded descent counts yields N(0,1/12), while a per-block covariance inequality summed over O(1) expected rare-event blocks gives mixed characteristic-functional factorization and independence. Exact finite covariance identities and overlap probabilities were independently enumerated with 140 and 20 rational checks. There is no claim that enumeration alone proves the limit.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary literature on maximal monotone blocks, rare increasing-run approximations, fixed-length joint permutation patterns, and classical descent limits supports the distinction: the accepted statement is a marked up/down spatial Poisson joint limit with independent Gaussian descent fluctuations. The statement is not obtained solely by combining previously stated marginal laws because independence is additional. Searches of the known own ledgers and published-result records found no covering claim. The unavailable full Chryssaphinou--Vaggelatou text and possible broad general joint-limit theorems remain explicit priority risks, not certified noncoverage.

value.rationale: Extreme locally monotone streaks are a standard nontrivial scan statistic, while the Eulerian descent count measures global directional disorder. The joint spatial theorem resolves their distinct multiscale dependence, including interaction between opposite orientations, event locations, and the global Gaussian count. Scalar longest-run or marginal descent laws do not determine this joint stochastic behavior. The exact nonzero finite covariances quantify the distinction and make the independence claim informative rather than a restatement of marginal Poisson and Gaussian convergence.
